milestoneContract.title: V6 PKG-A/PKG-A2 reviewed lock and Windows dependency-aware gate
milestoneContract.objective: Generate the reviewed package-lock on Node 24 / npm 11 and make canonical dependency-aware validation pass on Windows using only Founder-authorized minimum changes.
requirements: [PKG-A founderAuthorization.dependencyPinSet=APPROVED_ELECTRON_44_4_5_SET] Reviewed package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) for exactly these direct dependency changes: typescript 5.9.0 -> 5.9.3 (devDependencies); vitest 3.2.0 -> 4.1.11 (devDependencies); electron 38.0.0 -> 44.4.5 (devDependencies); fastify 5.6.0 -> 5.12.5 (dependencies); ajv 8.17.1 -> 8.20.0 (dependencies); tsx 4.20.0 -> 4.23.15 (devDependencies); unchanged: ajv-formats@3.0.1, concurrently@9.2.0, @types/node@24.0.0.

[PKG-A founderAuthorization.constraint] Minimum changes only; no weakening of trust, authority, reviewer isolation, evidence, provenance, Global Stop, security or fail-closed behavior; broader protected changes require separate Founder approval.

[PKG-A2 founderAuthorization.rule] A component that is not installed is accepted as PLATFORM_OPTIONAL_NOT_INSTALLED only if the lock marks it optional, its os/cpu/libc constraints provably exclude the current host, and it has sha512 integrity, an allowed registry URL and a lock license; every other component keeps the strict installed/license/packageJsonSha256 rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical validation (config/validation.json, all steps including dependency-supply-chain, release-supply-chain, typecheck and tests) passes on the exact reviewed commit on Windows with Node >=24 and npm >=11.

npm audit on the reviewed lock reports no moderate, high or critical vulnerability, and every lock entry resolves to https://registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity and no extraneous or link entries.

On Windows npm is never spawned as npm.cmd or with shell:true; it runs through node plus the npm-cli.js bundled beside the running node.exe and fails closed, without deleting node_modules, when that CLI is missing or not a regular file.

Release supply-chain accepts an uninstalled component only under the PKG-A2 founderAuthorization.rule; every other component keeps the strict installed/license/packageJsonSha256 rule, and host-matching uninstalled components stay blocking.
Only the Founder-authorized protected files change, and no existing test, assertion, validator or policy is weakened.
mandatoryFailureCases: optional component matching the host but not installed
optional flag forged only in the SBOM
